tb-E304-2.question:
Which of the following statements about non-renewable energy sources are correct?

(1) Greenhouse gases are produced when using these energy sources to generate electricity.

(2) They will be depleted.

(3) They are the main energy sources used to generate electricity globally.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-E304-2.reasoning: Editorial note: D is the supplied answer. Statement (1) is ambiguous because non-renewable sources include nuclear fuel. Nuclear generation itself does not emit greenhouse gases; with that interpretation, only (2) and (3) are correct (C). The original answer is retained here, with this qualification.

tb-E304-6.question:
In a hydroelectric power station, 3.30 × 1010 kg of water flows through a vertical distance of 200 m in 2 hours. Estimate the efficiency of the station if its average output power is 7 GW.

A 17.8%

B 56.1%

C 77.8%

D 87.5%
tb-E304-6.reasoning:
Energy input in 2 hours

= mgh

= 3.30 × 1010 × 9.81 × 200

= 6.4746 × 1013 J

Energy output in 2 hours

= Pt

= 7 × 109 × 2 × 3600

= 5.04 × 1013 J

Efficiency = 5.04 × 10136.4746 × 1013× 100%

= 77.8%

tb-E304-7.question:
The binding energy of a 37Li nucleus is 39.244 037 MeV. What is the mass of this nucleus?

Given: mass of proton = 1.007 276 u mass of neutron = 1.008 665 u

A 7.014 u

B 7.036 u

C 7.050 u

D 7.063 u
tb-E304-7.reasoning:
37Li consists of 3 protons and 4 neutrons.

Eb = ∆m × 931

39.244 037 = (3 × 1.007 276 +
4 × 1.008 665 − m) 931

m = 7.014 u

tb-E304-10.question:
A solar panel is illuminated by sunlight which is incident at an angle of 25° to the normal of the panel (Fig b) and the output power is 60 W.

What is the output power if the panel is turned by 30° clockwise as shown?

A 34 W

B 38 W

C 52 W

D 104 W
tb-E304-10.reasoning:
Let S be the power of solar radiation per unit area.

Power output P ∝ S cos θ ∝ cos θ

P2P1 = cos θ2cos θ1

P2 = cos θ2cos θ1P1

= cos(25°+30°)cos25°× 60

= 38 W

The energy sources used in a country for generating electricity are shown in Table a.

Coal

Gas

carbon dioxide, water

barium, krypton

(a) (i) Give two advantages of burning gas rather than coal in power stations. (2 marks)

tb-E304-18.question:
Figure e shows schematically the structure of a nuclear power station employing a pressurized water reactor.

(a) Explain the function of the moderator. (2 marks)

(b) Explain why pressurized water is pumped into the reactor core from the bottom and leaves it at the top. (2 marks)

(c) Why is the pressurized water prevented from mixing with the water in the steam generator? (1 mark)
tb-E304-18.answer:
(a) The moderator slows down the fast-moving neutrons produced by fission reactions, 1A

thus maintaining the chain reaction. 1A

(b) The water will be heated and rises when it flows through the reactor pressure vessel. 1A

If the water is pumped in the opposite direction, the convection current will be against the flow, making circulation less efficient. 1A

(c) The pressurized water may contain radioactive substances. It is not mixed with the water in the steam generator to prevent radioactive substances from leaking to the environment. 1A

source.name: E304 Revision 4 Energy Sources and Energy Consumption.docx

tb-E304-23.question:
Albert’s home has an average daily energy consumption of 30 kW h. Albert has installed some solar panels (Fig h) so that his home is entirely powered by solar power.

(a) Describe the working principle of a solar cell. (4 marks)

(b) The efficiency of the solar panels is 15%. Suppose the Sun shines for 10 hours each day and the average power of the solar radiation per unit area received by the solar panels is 800 W m–2 during this time period.

(i) What is the minimum area of solar panels required to meet Albert’s daily energy consumption? (2 marks)

(ii) In practice, an area larger than the result in (i) is needed. Give a reason for this. (1 mark)

(iii) What device, other than solar panels and cables, is needed to maintain the electricity supply at Albert’s home? (1 mark)
tb-E304-23.answer:
(a) In a solar cell, a layer of n-type semiconductor is attached to a layer of p-type semiconductor. 1A

This structure creates an electric field pointing from the n-side to the p-side at the p-n junction. 1A

When exposed to sunlight, an e.m.f. is set up across the two layers. 1A

A direct current is driven if it is in a complete circuit. 1A

(b) (i) Energy output = energy consumption

800A1000× 10 × 15% = 30 1M

A = 25 m2 1A

The minimum area of the solar panels is 25 m2.

(ii) Less solar radiation is received on cloudy days. 1A

(iii) Batteries are needed. 1A

source.name: E304 Revision 4 Energy Sources and Energy Consumption.docx

(a) Solar energy → electrical energy 1A

(b) Maximum solar power received

= 1366 × 1.2 × 10–4 × 106 1M

= 164 000 W 1A

(c) Maximum power output

= 164 000 × 20% 1M

= 32 800 W 1A

(d) It allows sunlight to fall normally onto the panel. 1A

(e) The batteries supply energy to the station when the station is in the shadow of the Earth. 1A

tb-E304-26.question:
In a pumped hydroelectric storage system (Fig i), the vertical distance between the water levels of the upper and lower reservoirs is 120 m and the turbine is below the water level of the lower reservoir.

(a) At night, electricity from a conventional power station is used to pump water from the lower reservoir to the upper reservoir. The efficiency in pumping water is 85%.

(i) State the energy conversion during this process. (1 mark)

(ii) If 2.8 × 108 kg of water is pumped to the upper reservoir in 1 hour, find the average input power provided to the system. (3 marks)

(b) During daytime, water from the upper reservoir flows through the turbine to generate electricity. Suggest why this system stores energy at night and generates electricity during daytime. (2 marks)

(c) A solar power station can work with a pumped hydroelectric storage system. What is the advantage in doing this? (2 marks)
tb-E304-26.answer:
(a) (i) Electrical energy

→ PE of water 1A

(ii) Average input power

= mghηt 1M

= 2.8 × 108 × 9.81 × 1200.85 × 3600

= 1.08 × 108 W 1A

(b) The demand of electricity is high during daytime and low at night. 1A

The power station stores the excess energy generated at night and helps to generate electricity to fulfil the high demand during daytime. 1A

(c) It levels the fluctuating output of solar power. 1A

Editorial correction: the average electrical input power in part (a)(ii) must include the pumping efficiency of 85%. The supplied solution calculated mgh/t = 9.16 × 10⁷ W; the corrected input power is mgh/(0.85t) = 1.08 × 10⁸ W.
